title: Apple and Raspberry Waffles
changes_from_base: A lighter batter made with milk, egg yolks and whisked whites folded in at the end, studded with diced apple and whole raspberries; served with maple syrup only.
summary: Fluffy whisked-egg-white waffles studded with diced apple and whole raspberries, best served fresh from the iron.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
apple, peeled, cored and cut into small dice (about 150 g)
unsalted butter, melted, plus a little for the iron

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Sift 125 g plain flour and 1 tsp baking powder into a large bowl with ⅛ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: Separate 2 eggs, keeping the whites in a clean bowl.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk the yolks with 240 ml milk, add to the dry mix and stir until just blended.

steps.title: Fold fruit
steps.text: Stir in 150 g diced apple and 95 g raspberries, then 28 g melted butter.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whisk the egg whites until stiff but not dry, then fold them gently into the batter.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Spoon about 120 ml batter per waffle into the hot iron, close and cook until browned and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve straight away with 60 ml maple syrup at the table.

tips: Dice the apple small so it cooks through in the time the waffle takes to crisp.
Fold the whisked egg whites in gently to keep the batter light and airy.
Only butter the iron if the waffles start to stick, as the batter already contains melted butter.
storage: These waffles are intended to be served straight away from the iron, so make them just before eating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
